parsed.explanation: The unit responds to several unrelated things: furry animal faces and bodies (dogs, chimpanzee, sloth bear, red panda) and assorted man-made gadgets (corkscrew, joystick base, clothes iron, old camera), plus scattered extras like a lobster, a custard apple and a parachute.
parsed.evidence: The three strongest images (activation 10) are a corkscrew, a joystick and an iron, while most of the 8-9 range is dark or furry mammal faces. No single visual feature (shape, texture or colour) connects these groups, and random images reach a moderate 4 on a gramophone and a furry animal.
parsed.missing_data: More top-activating examples, and activations on controlled sets (animal faces versus metallic or plastic gadgets), would show whether there are truly two separate features or one hidden low-level feature.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to a compact, roughly round mass in the middle of the frame with dense fine texture (fuzzy or tufted surfaces, often with a pair of small dark spots and soft fringes) that stands out sharply from its surroundings. It also responds, a little less, to rounded glossy or metallic forms with bright highlights and strong local light-dark contrast.
